subject.title: fix(infra): release exec-approvals locks across VirtioFS identity drift

question: Which single exec-approvals lock protocol should become the canonical fix for the VirtioFS sidecar-release failure: this hardened replay, the related live-proven PR, or a separately reviewed upstream fs-safe change?
rationale: The decision chooses a long-lived authorization-boundary implementation and determines whether this branch’s larger local protocol and extra hardening are worth adopting over the related live-proven path.

options.title: Adopt the live-proven canonical PR
options.body: Prefer https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028, then selectively port any narrowly reviewed hardening that is demonstrably absent there.

options.title: Adopt this hardened replay
options.body: Require an exact-head redacted VirtioFS deployment proof and a direct comparison explaining why its additional protocol complexity is necessary.

options.title: Move shared mechanics upstream
options.body: Pause both local implementations while defining and reviewing an fs-safe release that preserves OpenClaw’s fail-closed contract for all consumers.

recommendation.title: Adopt the live-proven canonical PR
recommendation.body: Prefer https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028, then selectively port any narrowly reviewed hardening that is demonstrably absent there.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the production reproduction and are the closest identifiable owner of the related live-proven implementation.
